name: restore_user_regs
prose: Restores a user mcontext into regs and current->thread. Returns 1 immediately, without calling user_read_access_end, if user_read_access_begin(sr, sizeof(*sr)) fails. After that every user read is a faulting accessor that jumps to the failed label on a fault; failed calls user_read_access_end and returns 1, leaving regs and current->thread partially updated. On success it calls user_read_access_end and returns 0. Steps: restore the general registers except MSR and SOFTE (via unsafe_restore_general_regs); when sig is 0 it saves gpr[2] beforehand and writes it back after the MSR word is read; it calls set_trap_norestart(regs) (the flag is set by that call, not read from sr); reads the saved msr from sr->mc_gregs[PT_MSR]; when sig is nonzero it copies only the MSR_LE bit of the saved msr into regs->msr. Under CONFIG_ALTIVEC it clears MSR_VEC in regs->msr, then if the saved msr has MSR_VEC copies sr->mc_vregs into current->thread.vr_state and sets used_vr true, otherwise zeroes vr_state only if used_vr is already true (used_vr is never cleared here); it then reads vrsave from sr and writes SPRN_VRSAVE if the CPU has CPU_FTR_ALTIVEC. It copies the FP registers from sr->mc_fregs. Under CONFIG_VSX it clears MSR_VSX in regs->msr, and if the saved msr has MSR_VSX copies the VSX state and sets used_vsr true, otherwise (only when used_vsr is already true) zeroes the low-offset half of the 32 fp_state entries. It clears MSR_FP, MSR_FE0 and MSR_FE1 in regs->msr. Under CONFIG_SPE it clears MSR_SPE, then if the saved msr has MSR_SPE copies sr->mc_vregs into current->thread.spe and sets used_spe true, otherwise zeroes thread.spe only if used_spe is already true, and reads spefscr from sr.
note: Reviewer 1 (used_vr/used_vsr never cleared) right, stated explicitly (signal_32.c:503-505,527-530). Reviewer 2 (CONFIG-conditional clears) right, prose now says under CONFIG_*. Reviewer 3 (trap norestart set not restored) right: set_trap_norestart(regs) at line 484 has no sr input. Slice cut the tail/head: real function is at 466-564.

name: start_contest
prose: Runs one timebase-contest round against a slave CPU that is waiting in the handshake protocol. It stores cmd in tbsync->cmd, then calls local_irq_disable(). The loop starts with i = -3 and runs while i < num, so when num <= -3 it never runs; otherwise it runs num+3 times. Each iteration publishes tbsync->tb and tbsync->mark from get_tb() plus offset, issues wmb(), sets tbsync->handshake to 1, spins until tbsync->ack is zero, spins until get_tb() passes tb, clears tbsync->handshake, calls enter_contest(mark, 1), and spins until tbsync->ack is nonzero. After the wait it adds tbsync->race_result to the score only if the pre-increment value of i was greater than 0 (i takes the values -3 up to num-1, so the sampled iterations are i = 1..num-1). It then calls local_irq_enable() unconditionally (it does not restore previously saved flags) and returns the score. The return is 0 when num <= 1; the code does not constrain the range of race_result. The loops are unbounded busy waits that depend on the slave responding.
note: Reviewer 1 (formal contract) moot, contract left empty. Reviewer 2 (handshake/ack fail when num<=-3) right, prose says loop never runs then. Reviewer 3 (irqs not restored) right: smp-tbsync.c:86,109 use local_irq_disable/local_irq_enable with no saved flags. Dropped the unverified +-1 and parity claims; they depend on race_result values not shown (tbsync stores unverified).

name: __cpu_up
prose: Brings up secondary CPU cpu using idle task tidle via smp_ops. Returns -EBUSY if threads_per_core > 1, secondaries_inhibited() is true and cpu_thread_in_subcore(cpu) is true. Returns -EINVAL if smp_ops is NULL, or if smp_ops->cpu_bootable exists and returns false for cpu. Otherwise it calls cpu_idle_thread_init, which (under CONFIG_PPC64) sets paca_ptrs[cpu]->__current and ->kstack, and in all configs sets task_thread_info(idle)->cpu and secondary_current and current_set[cpu] to tidle. If smp_ops->prepare_cpu exists and returns nonzero, that value is returned (the idle-thread initialization has already happened). It then sets cpu_callin_map[cpu] to 0, calls smp_mb(), and calls smp_ops->kick_cpu(cpu); a nonzero result is logged and returned. Next it spins until cpu_callin_map[cpu] is nonzero or a deadline passes (5 s if system_state < SYSTEM_RUNNING, else 1 ms); if still not called in and system_state >= SYSTEM_RUNNING it additionally sleeps in 10 ms steps (fsleep) until call-in or a 100 s deadline. If cpu_callin_map[cpu] is still zero it logs an error and returns -ENOENT. Otherwise it calls smp_ops->give_timebase() if non-NULL, spins (with no timeout) until cpu_online(cpu) is true, and returns 0.
note: Reviewer 1 (omits callin-map side effect) addressed. Reviewer 2 (idle init ordering) already correct: smp.c:1291 precedes prepare_cpu at 1297. Reviewer 3 (100 s sleep loop does not exist) WRONG: smp.c:1332-1339 has a runtime sleep loop with sleep_wait_ms = 100*MSEC_PER_SEC. Slice cut head; real function at 1271-1355.

name: kvmppc_run_vcpu
prose: Runs vcpu inside its virtual core. It sets run->exit_reason to 0, vcpu->arch.ret to RESUME_GUEST and arch.trap to 0, calls kvmppc_update_vpas, takes vc->lock, marks the vcpu KVMPPC_VCPU_RUNNABLE, records it in vc->runnable_threads and increments vc->n_runnable. If no signal is pending it either starts the thread on an already running/piggyback vcore (when not exiting) or wakes the vcore wait if sleeping. It then loops while the vcpu is runnable and no signal is pending: if the VM's MMU is not ready it drops vc->lock to call kvmhv_setup_mmu; a nonzero result r sets run->exit_reason to KVM_EXIT_FAIL_ENTRY, fail_entry.hardware_entry_failure_reason to 0, vcpu->arch.ret to r and leaves the loop. Otherwise it waits for or ends preemption, signals/removes other runnable threads with pending signals (setting their ret to -EINTR), and either blocks, yields, or calls kvmppc_run_core. It then waits (uninterruptibly) while the vcore is running/exiting/piggybacking. If the vcpu is still KVMPPC_VCPU_RUNNABLE at that point it is removed from the runnable set, signal_exits is incremented, run->exit_reason is set to KVM_EXIT_INTR and vcpu->arch.ret to -EINTR; this also overwrites the value from a kvmhv_setup_mmu failure, because the failure path leaves the vcpu runnable (so the MMU error is normally not what is returned, though run->fail_entry fields stay set). If runnable threads remain and the vcore is inactive, one is woken. There is a single return: it releases vc->lock and returns vcpu->arch.ret.
note: Reviewer (MMU failure overwritten with -EINTR/KVM_EXIT_INTR) RIGHT: book3s_hv.c:4803-4808 break leaves state RUNNABLE, then 4862-4867 sets ret=-EINTR and exit_reason=KVM_EXIT_INTR. Slice cut the head; real function at 4751-4879.

name: kvmppc_vcpu_run_hv
prose: Top-level KVM_RUN handler for a HV vcpu. Early returns before any state change: if vcpu->arch.sane is false it sets run->exit_reason to KVM_EXIT_INTERNAL_ERROR and returns -EINVAL; if a signal is pending it sets KVM_EXIT_INTR and returns -EINTR; under CONFIG_PPC_TRANSACTIONAL_MEM, if the CPU has CPU_FTR_TM, current->thread.regs exists with MSR_TM set and MSR_TM_ACTIVE is true, it sets KVM_EXIT_FAIL_ENTRY with hardware_entry_failure_reason 0 and returns -EINVAL (when MSR_TM is set but not active, execution continues). Otherwise it sets vcpu->arch.online to 1 (incrementing vcore->online_count if it was 0), calls kvmppc_core_prepare_to_enter, increments kvm->arch.vcpus_running, sets MSR bits for FP, VEC, VSX and TM according to config/CPU features via msr_check_and_set, saves user registers and SPRs, and sets arch.state to KVMPPC_VCPU_BUSY_IN_HOST. It then loops, calling kvmhv_run_single_vcpu (CPU_FTR_ARCH_300) or kvmppc_run_vcpu, and handling a PAPR hcall exit (kvmppc_pseries_do_hcall, or r = RESUME_GUEST and continue when the hypervisor-MSR_PR sanity check fires), RESUME_PAGE_FAULT (kvmppc_book3s_hv_page_fault under srcu) and RESUME_PASSTHROUGH, until is_kvmppc_resume_guest(r) is false. It then sets arch.state to KVMPPC_VCPU_NOTREADY, decrements vcpus_running and returns r, which is the last value from the loop and by the loop condition is not a resume-guest code (it is not RESUME_GUEST, which equals 0, or RESUME_GUEST_NV).
note: Reviewer 1 (omits TM -EINVAL) already covered. Reviewer 2 (H_SUCCESS is 0, final can be zero) WRONG for the return: zero is RESUME_GUEST (kvm_asm.h:141) and keeps the do-while looping (5209); prose earlier allowed 0. Reviewer 3 (final is never a resume-guest code) right. Slice cut head; real function at 5098-5220.

name: kvmppc_booke_init
prose: Init function. When CONFIG_KVM_BOOKE_HV is set the body is empty and it returns 0. Otherwise it allocates a zeroed block of VCPU_SIZE_ORDER pages with __get_free_pages(GFP_KERNEL | __GFP_ZERO) into kvmppc_booke_handlers and returns -ENOMEM (-12) if that fails, with no other effect. On success it reads the 16 host IVOR SPRs, and for each i in 0..15 copies handler[i+1]-handler[i] bytes from kvmppc_booke_handler_addr[i] to kvmppc_booke_handlers + ivor[i]. It then calls flush_icache_range from kvmppc_booke_handlers up to kvmppc_booke_handlers + ivor[max_ivor] + the length of handler max_ivor, and returns 0. max_ivor is updated as max_ivor = i whenever ivor[i] > max_ivor (an index is stored in a variable compared against addresses), so the flushed range is based on that index and is not guaranteed to cover the copy at the largest IVOR offset. The allocated block is not freed on any path in this function.
note: Reviewer (flush range may not cover all handlers) RIGHT: booke.c:2223-2224 stores i, not ivor[i], in max_ivor, and the flush at 2231-2233 uses ivor[max_ivor]. Contract removed (function touches global state and allocates). Slice cut head; real function at 2185-2236.

name: kvmppc_booke_emulate_mtspr
prose: Emulates a guest mtspr of spr_val to SPR sprn for a Book-E vcpu. It switches on sprn: DEAR and ESR are stored into vcpu->arch.shared->dar/esr; CSRR0/1 and DSRR0/1 into vcpu->arch.csrr0/csrr1/dsrr0/dsrr1; DECAR into vcpu->arch.decar; SPRG4-7 through kvmppc_set_sprg4..7; IVPR into vcpu->arch.ivpr (and mtspr GIVPR when CONFIG_KVM_BOOKE_HV); IVOR0-15 into the matching vcpu->arch.ivor[BOOKE_IRQPRIO_*] entry (and mtspr GIVOR2 / GIVOR8 for IVOR2 / IVOR8 in HV builds); MCSR clears the bits set in spr_val; TSR clears bits via kvmppc_clr_tsr_bits; TCR is passed to kvmppc_set_tcr after preserving the existing TCR_WRC_MASK bits if any are set in vcpu->arch.tcr; on CONFIG_64BIT EPCR calls kvmppc_set_epcr (plus mtspr EPCR with shadow_epcr in HV builds). For IAC1, IAC2, DAC1, DAC2, DBCR0, DBCR1, DBCR2 (and IAC3/IAC4 when CONFIG_PPC_ADV_DEBUG_IACS > 2) and for DBSR, the write is skipped (break) if vcpu->guest_debug is nonzero; otherwise the register is stored (DBCR0 masked to IDM, IC, BT, TIE, IAC1-4 and DAC1/2 R/W bits), the debug_inst flag is set for all of these except DBSR, and DBSR clears the written bits from vcpu->arch.dbsr and calls kvmppc_core_dequeue_debug if no bits other than DBSR_IDE remain. Unrecognised sprn sets the result to EMULATE_FAIL. After the switch, if debug_inst is set it copies vcpu->arch.dbg_reg into current->thread.debug and calls switch_booke_debug_regs. It returns EMULATE_DONE for every recognised sprn (including the ignored guest_debug cases) and EMULATE_FAIL otherwise.
note: Reviewer (DBSR writes not ignored when guest_debug set) WRONG: booke_emulate.c case SPRN_DBSR (lines ~239-247 of file, after DBCR2) has 'if (vcpu->guest_debug) break;' before the dbsr update; it is the other registers' debug_inst flag that DBSR does not set. Prose rewritten more precisely. Slice cut head; real function at 120-377.

name: kvmppc_emulate_loadstore
prose: Emulates a trapped guest load/store instruction through MMIO. It first calls kvmppc_set_exit_type(vcpu, EMULATED_INST_EXITS), then kvmppc_get_last_inst(vcpu, INST_GENERIC, &inst); if that does not return EMULATE_DONE it returns that value at once (the exit type has already been set). Otherwise it zeroes the vcpu->arch.mmio_* copy/offset/extend/swab fields (setting mmio_copy_type to KVMPPC_VSX_COPY_NONE), loads vcpu->arch.regs.msr from kvmppc_get_msr, and calls analyse_instr; if it returns nonzero no handler is called and the result stays EMULATE_FAIL. Otherwise it sets vcpu->mmio_is_write for stores and switches on the instruction type. LOAD, STORE, LOAD_FP and STORE_FP (the FP ones under CONFIG_PPC_FPU) call kvmppc_handle_load[s]/kvmppc_handle_store and then, if the UPDATE bit is set and the handler did not return EMULATE_FAIL, write vcpu->arch.vaddr_accessed to GPR op.update_reg; this update is not done for the VMX and VSX cases. LOAD_VMX/STORE_VMX (CONFIG_ALTIVEC) align vaddr_accessed/paddr_accessed down to the size, support sizes 1, 2, 4 and 16 (other sizes leave the result EMULATE_FAIL) and call kvmppc_handle_vmx_load/store; LOAD_VSX/STORE_VSX (CONFIG_VSX) support element_size 4 or 8 (otherwise EMULATE_FAIL) and call kvmppc_handle_vsx_load/store. The store cases may call kvm_ops->giveup_ext first. CACHEOP sets EMULATE_DONE and any other type leaves EMULATE_FAIL. The FP/VMX/VSX cases return EMULATE_DONE immediately when the corresponding kvmppc_check_*_disabled call returns true, skipping the trace event and the PC advance. Otherwise it emits trace_kvm_ppc_instr and, if the result is not EMULATE_FAIL, advances the PC by the instruction length, then returns the result (the handler's return value or EMULATE_FAIL / EMULATE_DONE as above).
note: Reviewer 1 (analyse_instr failure / bad VMX-VSX sizes return FAIL without handler) right and stated. Reviewer 3 (kvmppc_set_exit_type called before get_last_inst) RIGHT: emulate_loadstore.c:79. Old prose also overstated UPDATE handling (applies only to LOAD, LOAD_FP, STORE, STORE_FP: lines 113,133,~235,~255); corrected. Slice cut head; real function at 72-367.

name: __kvmppc_handle_load
prose: Starts an MMIO load of bytes bytes for the vcpu into register rt. It first computes a local host_swabbed: if kvmppc_need_byteswap(vcpu) is true it equals is_default_endian, otherwise it equals !is_default_endian (an XNOR of the two). If bytes > sizeof(run->mmio.data) it returns EMULATE_FAIL at that point; no vcpu or run state has been modified up to there (the code does not set GPR rt). Otherwise it fills run->mmio (phys_addr from vcpu->arch.paddr_accessed, len = bytes, is_write = 0), sets vcpu->arch.io_gpr = rt, vcpu->arch.mmio_host_swabbed = host_swabbed, vcpu->mmio_needed = 1, vcpu->mmio_is_write = 0 and vcpu->arch.mmio_sign_extend = sign_extend, then under srcu_read_lock(&vcpu->kvm->srcu) calls kvm_io_bus_read on KVM_MMIO_BUS for the physical address. If that returns 0 it calls kvmppc_complete_mmio_load, sets vcpu->mmio_needed = 0 and returns EMULATE_DONE; otherwise it returns EMULATE_DO_MMIO with mmio_needed left at 1 so that userspace must supply the data.
note: Reviewer 1 (XNOR not XOR) right and stated (powerpc.c:1258-1262). Reviewer 3 (bytes too large sets GPR rt to 0) WRONG for this source: powerpc.c:1264-1265 returns EMULATE_FAIL with no GPR write. Slice cut head; real function at 1249-1291.

name: test_prefix_word_alt_patching
prose: Self-test that runs only in a CONFIG_PPC64 build (the non-64-bit variant is an empty stub). It takes no arguments and returns void. It sets the file-level fixup entry itself: value and mask are set to 8, start_off/end_off to the offsets of ftr_fixup_prefix3+1 and +4 (three words), and alt_start_off/alt_end_off to the offsets of ftr_fixup_prefix3_alt and +3 (also three words). It then runs check() that the ftr_fixup_prefix3 buffer (size computed from end_ftr_fixup_prefix3) equals ftr_fixup_prefix3_orig, calls patch_feature_section(0, &fixup) and checks the buffer equals ftr_fixup_prefix3_expected, calls patch_feature_section(0, &fixup) again and checks only that the buffer differs from ftr_fixup_prefix3_orig (the second result is not compared with the expected image). check() only prints a printk message with the line number when its condition is false; it does not abort or return a status.
note: Reviewer 1 (second patch checked only against orig) right, stated (feature-fixups.c:990). Reviewer 2 (span counts) right: 3 words each. Reviewer 3 (precondition wrong, function sets fixup itself) RIGHT (979-983). Slice cut head; real function at 970-991; check() defined at 709-710.

name: do_spe_mathemu
prose: Emulates one e500 SPE floating-point instruction at regs->nip. Return paths: -EFAULT if get_user of the instruction word fails; -EINVAL if the primary opcode is not EFAPU or if the instruction's src field (bits 5..7) matches none of the handled floating-point formats (the final default of the outer switch); -ENOSYS (after a printk) via the illegal label when insn_type returns NOTYPE or the func code is unsupported within its format, except that when have_e500_cpu_a005_erratum is set the illegal path calls regs_add_return_ip(regs, -4) to re-issue the instruction and returns 0 instead. On the normal path it loads the operands from current->thread.evr[] and regs->gpr[], reads SPEFSCR, performs the operation with the soft-float macros and either packs the result, stores it, or computes a compare result into IR and merges it into the selected regs->ccr field (update_ccr); at update_regs it merges the current exceptions into SPEFSCR (clearing invalid/underflow sticky bits that were not set in spefscr_last), writes SPEFSCR with mtspr, saves spefscr_last, and writes the result vc to current->thread.evr[fc] and regs->gpr[fc] (also for compares). It then returns 1 if current->thread.fpexc_mode has PR_FP_EXC_SW_ENABLE and a current exception (divide by zero, overflow, underflow, inexact, invalid) has its matching PR_FP_EXC_* enable bit set, and otherwise returns 0.
note: Reviewer (unsupported func/opcode goes to illegal and returns -ENOSYS, not -EINVAL) RIGHT for NOTYPE and unsupported func (math_efp.c:191-192,322,464,623,714-723), while -EINVAL still exists for a non-SPE primary opcode (188) and unknown src (655). Old prose also attributed -ENOSYS to type XCR, which is in speround_handler (741), not here. Slice 509-759 is only part of do_spe_mathemu (177-725) plus the head of speround_handler; name was missing from the slice.

name: ___tlbie
prose: Issues a tlbie for the given vpn and returns the encoded address it used. It starts with va = vpn << VPN_SHIFT, and if mmu_has_feature(MMU_FTR_TLBIE_CROP_VA) clears the top 16 bits. For psize == MMU_PAGE_4K it clears the low 12 bits of va, ORs in ssize << 8 and get_sllp_encoding(apsize) << 5, and executes tlbie with L=0 (on CPUs without CPU_FTR_ARCH_206 via the PPC_TLBIE alternative). For any other psize it reads penc = mmu_psize_defs[psize].penc[apsize], clears the low mmu_psize_defs[apsize].shift bits of va (the shift is taken from the apsize entry), ORs in penc << 12, ssize << 8, (vpn & 0xfe) and the L bit 1, and executes tlbie with L=1. In both cases the instruction is issued with a memory clobber, and the function then returns that va. It takes no locks and has no early return; the caller is responsible for the surrounding synchronization.
note: Reviewers 1-3 criticised the formal contract (psize/apsize bounds, missing return/lock claims); the contract is removed because the function reads global mmu_psize_defs and executes inline asm. Return claims in old prose are consistent with hash_native.c:94-115 but not needed. Slice cut head; real function at 67-122.

name: hash__change_memory_range
prose: Changes the hash-MMU page protection of the linear-mapped range [start, end) to newpp. It computes step = 1 << mmu_psize_defs[mmu_linear_psize].shift, rounds start down and end up to step, and if the rounded start >= end it returns false with nothing changed. Otherwise, if firmware_has_feature(FW_FEATURE_LPAR) is true it takes the mutex chmem_lock, stores start, end, step and newpp in chmem_parms, sets master_cpu to 0, takes cpus_read_lock, sets cpu_counter to num_online_cpus(), issues mb(), calls stop_machine_cpuslocked(change_memory_range_fn, &chmem_parms, cpu_online_mask) (its return value is ignored), then releases cpus_read_lock and chmem_lock. If not LPAR it calls change_memory_range(start, end, step, newpp) directly with no lock taken here. After either path it returns true, so the return value does not report a stop_machine failure.
note: Reviewer 3 (LPAR path returns rc==0, not always true) WRONG: hash_pgtable.c:529-537 ignores the stop_machine_cpuslocked result and returns true. Reviewers 1/2 targeted the old contract (removed; internal chmem_lock locking at 514/533 confirmed). Prose details of change_memory_range_fn omitted since not read. Slice cut head; real function at 499-538.

name: hpte_insert_repeating
prose: Inserts an HPTE for vpn into the hash table, retrying until a slot is obtained. The primary group is (hash & htab_hash_mask) * HPTES_PER_GROUP; it calls mmu_hash_ops.hpte_insert there with psize for both page-size arguments. If that returns -1 it tries the secondary group ((~hash & htab_hash_mask) * HPTES_PER_GROUP) with HPTE_V_SECONDARY ORed into vflags. If the secondary insert also returns -1 it picks the secondary group, or the primary group when the low bit of mftb() is set, calls mmu_hash_ops.hpte_remove on that group (its result is not examined) and jumps back to repeat to try the whole sequence again; this loop has no iteration limit. Whenever either hpte_insert call returns anything other than -1 (the slot, or another error value the callback might return) that value is returned. The function never returns -1 itself.
note: Reviewer 1 (can return -1 when hpte_remove fails) WRONG: hash_utils.c:2302-2303 ignores hpte_remove result and always loops back. Reviewers 2 and 3 (eviction only from secondary group) WRONG: lines 2298-2300 switch hpte_group to the primary group when mftb() & 1. Formal contract removed (function reads globals htab_hash_mask and mmu_hash_ops; callback results other than -1 may still be negative). Slice cut head; real function at 2277-2308.

name: bpf_jit_emit_tail_call
prose: Emits 32-bit PowerPC code for a BPF tail call and returns 0, or returns -ERANGE from inside the PPC_BCC_SHORT macro if a conditional branch to out is not within range of the generated branch instruction (three branch sites; the macro also logs a rate-limited error). The code it emits expects the BPF context pointer in r3-r4, the bpf_array pointer in r5-r6 and the index in r7-r8. The emitted sequence loads array->map.max_entries into r0 and compares it with the index (CMPLW), loads the tail-call counter from the BPF_PPC_TC stack slot into r0 (this load is emitted before the first conditional branch, so it runs in both outcomes), and branches to out if index >= max_entries. It then compares r0 with MAX_TAIL_CALL_CNT (CMPLWI), emits ADDIC r0,r0,1 (the increment), and branches to out if the compare result (made on the pre-increment counter) was >= MAX_TAIL_CALL_CNT. It then loads array->ptrs[index] into r3 and branches to out if it is zero; otherwise it loads prog->bpf_func, adds BPF_TAILCALL_PROLOGUE_SIZE, moves it to CTR, restores r3 from the BPF context register, puts the incremented counter in r4, calls bpf_jit_emit_common_epilogue (restoring registers and tearing down the frame) and emits BCTR. The out label itself is not emitted here.
note: Reviewer 1 (precondition says r3-r6 hold index) right and fixed. Reviewer 2 (branch tests CMPLWI result) right and stated. Reviewer 3 (counter loaded before max_entries branch) right: bpf_jit_comp32.c:243 precedes branch at 244. Prior 'always returns 0' wrong: PPC_BCC_SHORT can return -ERANGE (net/bpf_jit.h:44-52). Slice cut head; real function at 226-284.

name: bpf_jit_build_body
prose: Emits PowerPC64 machine code for every instruction of the BPF program fp (fp->len instructions) into the codegen context ctx. It reads exit_addr from addrs[flen], then loops over the instructions; at the top of every iteration it sets addrs[i] = ctx->idx * 4 (so the entry for the instruction being processed is written before any failure return), and marks the destination and source registers as seen when they are non-volatile PPC registers. Some instructions advance i themselves (storing addrs[++i] = ctx->idx * 4 for the folded following instruction). The switch handles the ALU, jump, load/store, atomic, call, tail-call and exit opcodes. Return values: -EINVAL when a DIV/MOD by-immediate has imm == 0; -1 when sign_extend fails or prepare_for_kfunc_call fails; a negative ret propagated from bpf_jit_emit_probe_mem_store, bpf_add_extable_entry, bpf_jit_emit_atomic_ops (other than the -EOPNOTSUPP case, which is checked separately), emit_atomic_ld_st, bpf_jit_emit_exit_insn, bpf_jit_get_func_addr, bpf_jit_emit_func_call_rel or bpf_jit_emit_tail_call (the last is tested with ret < 0); -EOPNOTSUPP for an unsupported atomic size; and -ENOTSUPP after a rate-limited error print for an unsupported opcode. A BPF_TAIL_CALL sets SEEN_TAILCALL in ctx->seen before emitting. If the loop ends without error it stores addrs[i] = ctx->idx * 4 (the end-of-body offset, with i == flen unless folded instructions advanced it) and returns 0. On a failing return, code for earlier instructions has already been emitted into ctx/image.
note: Reviewer (failure paths return before writing addrs[i]) WRONG: bpf_jit_comp64.c:741 writes addrs[i] at the start of each iteration, before the switch and before every failure return in the body. Old prose omitted several return sources (-EOPNOTSUPP at ~1295, atomic/probe helpers) which are listed now. Slice cut head; real function at 709-1720 (1,000+ lines), only returns and addrs writes checked, not each opcode's emitted sequence.

name: create_events_from_catalog
prose: Builds the sysfs event attribute arrays from the 24x7 catalog. It allocates catalog page 0 from hv_page_cache and fetches it with h_get_24x7_catalog_page. Failures: -ENOMEM if the page allocation, the vmalloc of the event data, or any of the three kmalloc_array calls fails; -EIO if fetching catalog page 0 fails, if the page count exceeds MAX_4K, if event_data_offs/event_data_len are out of range or do not fit inside the catalog, if event_entry_count > SIZE_MAX - 1, or if fetching any event-data page fails (each failure path frees what it had allocated, and sets *events_, *event_descs_ and *event_long_descs_ to NULL). It then scans the event data once with catalog_event_len_validate; a validation failure (negative length) does not cause an error return: it ends the scan early, and the code only prints a warning if the number of events parsed differs from event_entry_count. Events that are ignored, have group_record_len == 0 or an invalid domain are counted as junk and skipped. After the arrays are allocated (events sized attr_max + 1, event_descs and event_long_descs sized event_idx + 1) it fills them in a second pass (skipping the same junk events; events whose attribute creation fails are skipped with a warning). On success it NULL-terminates the three arrays, destroys the uniqueness tree, frees the event data and the catalog page, stores the arrays in the three output pointers and returns 0.
note: Reviewer (catalog_event_len_validate failure breaks the scan and can still return 0) RIGHT: hv-24x7.c scan loop 'if (ev_len < 0) break;' followed only by a pr_warn. Old prose claimed -EIO for event-data validation failure; fixed. Slice cut head and name; real function create_events_from_catalog at 754-998.

name: find_alternative_bdecode
prose: Pure function (s64 find_alternative_bdecode(u64 event)) that computes an alternative event code for a POWER5+ event. It extracts pmc = (event >> PM_PMC_SH) & PM_PMC_MSK and returns -1 if pmc is 0 or greater than 4. Otherwise altpmc = 5 - pmc and pp = event & PM_PMCSEL_MSK. If pp equals one of the four entries of bytedecode_alternatives[pmc-1], it returns event with the PMC and PMCSEL fields cleared and replaced by altpmc and the entry bytedecode_alternatives[altpmc-1][j] in the same column j. Else, if pmc == 1 and pp is 0x0d or 0x0e, it returns event + (2 << PM_PMC_SH) + 0x21 (PMC becomes 3 and PMCSEL 0x2e or 0x2f); else if pmc == 3 and pp is 0x2e or 0x2f it returns event - (2 << PM_PMC_SH) - 0x21. Else, if pp is 0x10 or 0x28 (the add-event encodings), it returns the event with PMCSEL toggled between 0x10 and 0x28 (xor with 0x38), the PMC mask bits cleared and the PMC field set to altpmc. Otherwise it returns -1. It has no side effects.
note: Reviewers 1 and 2 (add-event alternatives omitted) RIGHT: power5+-pmu.c:266-269 handles pp 0x10/0x28. Reviewer 3: formal contract syntax; contract cleared. Slice cut head; real function at 243-272.

name: find_alternative_bdecode
prose: Pure function (s64 find_alternative_bdecode(u64 event)) that computes an alternative event code for a POWER5 event. It extracts pmc = (event >> PM_PMC_SH) & PM_PMC_MSK and returns -1 if pmc is 0 or greater than 4. Otherwise altpmc = 5 - pmc (1<->4, 2<->3) and pp = event & PM_PMCSEL_MSK. If pp equals one of the four entries of bytedecode_alternatives[pmc-1], it returns event with the PMC and PMCSEL fields cleared and replaced by altpmc and the entry bytedecode_alternatives[altpmc-1][j] in the same column j. If pp matches none of the four entries it returns -1. It has no side effects.
note: Reviewer 1 (formal contract excludes PMC4, compares pmc to altpmc-1) concerns the old contract, cleared. Reviewer 15 (contract syntax) moot. Code checked at power5-pmu.c:251-268. Slice cut head.

name: init_ppc970_pmu
prose: Reads the PVR SPR. If PVR_VER(pvr) is none of PVR_970, PVR_970MP, PVR_970FX or PVR_970GX it returns -ENODEV without registering anything. Otherwise it calls register_power_pmu(&ppc970_pmu) and returns that call's result unchanged (0 on success, or whatever negative error code register_power_pmu returns). This registers the PPC970 PMU description with the powerpc perf code as a side effect.
note: Reviewer 15 (does more than read PVR) right; prose now states the register_power_pmu side effect. Code checked at ppc970-pmu.c:492-501. Slice cut head.

name: mpc512x_cs_config
prose: Writes val to the cs_cfg register for chip select cs of the MPC5121 local-plus-bus controller. If cs > 7 it returns -EINVAL with no mapping attempted and no write. The controller's register block is mapped lazily through a static pointer lpc: if lpc is NULL it finds the node compatible with fsl,mpc5121-lpc, calls of_iomap(np, 0) and of_node_put(np); if the mapping is NULL it returns -ENOMEM without writing (lpc stays NULL, so any later call with cs <= 7 tries the mapping again, not only the first). Otherwise it does out_be32(&lpc->cs_cfg[cs], val) and returns 0. The static pointer is updated without any locking.
note: Reviewer (contract omits cached mapping/retry and no-write on error) right; contract removed (static state). Old prose said failure 'can only happen on the first call', which is wrong: it can repeat on every call while the node is missing or the map fails. Code checked at mpc512x_shared.c:487-505.

name: pdm360ng_penirq_init
prose: Init function that sets up the pen interrupt GPIO registers. It looks up a node compatible with fsl,mpc5121-gpio; if none is found it prints an error and returns -ENODEV without touching pdm360ng_gpio_base. Otherwise it assigns pdm360ng_gpio_base = of_iomap(np, 0) (so the pointer becomes NULL if the mapping fails), calls of_node_put(np), and if the pointer is NULL prints an error and returns -ENODEV. On success it writes 0xffffffff to the register at offset 0xc, sets bit 0x2000 at offset 0x18 and bit 0x40 at offset 0x10 (setbits32), and returns 0; the mapping is kept in pdm360ng_gpio_base and is not unmapped by this function.
note: Reviewer (of_iomap failure sets pdm360ng_gpio_base to NULL) RIGHT: pdm360ng.c:61-66; prose states it. Contract removed (writes a global). Slice cut head; real function at 51-72.

name: cpm_command
prose: Issues a command to the CPM command register. If (command & 0xffffff03) is nonzero (any of bits 0, 1 or 8 through 31 set) it returns -EINVAL before taking the lock. Otherwise it takes cmd_lock with spin_lock_irqsave, writes command | CPM_CR_FLG | (opcode << 8) to cpmp->cp_cpcr with out_be16, and polls that register up to MAX_CR_CMD_LOOPS (10000) times for CPM_CR_FLG to read as zero. If the flag clears the result is 0; if not, it prints an error with printk and the result is -EIO. In both cases it then releases cmd_lock with spin_unlock_irqrestore and returns the result.
note: Contract removed: function writes hardware registers. No reviewer claims in the history beyond mechanical contract-mismatch ones. Code checked at cpm1.c:89-110. Slice cut head.

name: do_fail_paste
prose: Makes a faulting user-mode paste instruction appear to fail. It takes current->thread.regs. Returns -EINVAL (after WARN_ON_ONCE) if that pointer is NULL, or if user_mode(regs) is false. Then it does get_user(instword, regs->nip) and returns -EAGAIN if that fails. If (instword & PPC_INST_PASTE_MASK) != PPC_INST_PASTE it returns -ENOENT. Otherwise it clears CR0 bits 0-2 (regs->ccr &= ~0xe0000000), advances the return IP by 4 with regs_add_return_ip, and returns 0. On every non-zero return the registers are unmodified; no lock or reference is taken.
note: Contract removed (touches thread registers). No substantive reviewer disagreement; code checked at vas-api.c:359-388. Slice cut head.

name: smp_core99_kick_cpu
prose: Starts secondary CPU nr on a Core99 PowerMac. If nr < 0 or nr > 3 it returns -ENOENT immediately. Otherwise it calls ppc_md.progress if that pointer is set, saves the IRQ state with local_irq_save, saves the word at PAGE_OFFSET+0x100, patches that word with a linking branch to __secondary_start_pmac_0 + nr*8 (patch_branch with BRANCH_SET_LINK), calls pmac_call_feature(PMAC_FTR_RESET_CPU, NULL, nr, 0) (its result is ignored), waits 1 ms with mdelay, restores the saved word with patch_uint, restores the IRQ state, calls ppc_md.progress again if set, and returns 0.
note: Reviewers (precondition 'no restriction' wrong; formal omits side effects) RIGHT; old prose now fixed and contract removed. Code at smp.c:796-836.

name: power9_idle_stop
prose: Enters a POWER9 stop state with PSSCR psscr and returns the SRR1 wake value, after executing mtmsr(MSR_KERNEL) on the common exit. If neither PSSCR_EC nor PSSCR_ESL is set it calls isa300_idle_stop_noloss; a zero SRR1 returns 0 directly (without the mtmsr); a nonzero SRR1 triggers BUG_ON unless the wake state is SRR1_WS_NOLOSS, and then jumps to out and returns that SRR1. Otherwise (EC=ESL=1), under CONFIG_KVM_BOOK3S_HV_POSSIBLE with CPU_FTR_P9_TM_XER_SO_BUG it sets local_paca->requested_psscr, and if local_paca->dont_stop is set it clears requested_psscr and returns 0. It saves MMCR0 on CPUs without POWER9_DD2_1; if the PSSCR RL field is at least deep_spr_loss_state it saves a set of SPRs into a local struct and calls atomic_start_thread_idle; it saves AMR/IAMR/UAMOR, calls isa300_idle_stop_mayloss, clears requested_psscr, re-reads PSSCR and WARNs once if SRR1 was 0 (SRR1 is still returned, so 0 is possible in this branch). If the wake state is not SRR1_WS_NOLOSS it restores AMR, IAMR, UAMOR, sets AMOR to ~0, and (for pre-DD2.1) invalidates the ERAT and restores MMCR0, then sets and clears MMCRA bit 60. It calls hmi_exception_realmode(NULL) for an HMI wake. If the post-wake PSSCR PLS is below deep_spr_loss_state it calls atomic_stop_thread_idle when SPRs were saved and goes to out. Otherwise it locks thread idle state; if another thread of the core is still marked in the idle state it skips the per-core SPR restore and timebase resync (goto core_woken), else restores PTCR, RPR and TSCR, resynchronises the timebase via opal_resync_timebase (BUG on failure) when pls >= pnv_first_tb_loss_level, and executes isync. At core_woken it unlocks, restores the per-thread SPRs (LPCR, HFSCR, FSCR, PID, PURR, SPURR, DSCR, CIABR, MMCRA, MMCR0-2, LDBAR if not ultravisor, SPRG3), restores the bolted SLB if not radix, and falls to out.
note: Reviewer 1 (EC=ESL=0 can return nonzero NOLOSS) right. Reviewer 2 (EC=ESL=1 can return 0 after WARN) right (idle.c:~700). Reviewer 3 (per-core SPRs restored on core_woken path too) WRONG: goto core_woken skips PTCR/RPR/TSCR restore and TB resync; only per-thread SPRs are restored on both paths. Slice cut head; real function at 608-805.

name: opal_async_comp_init
prose: Init function for the OPAL async-completion machinery, no arguments. It looks up /ibm,opal; if absent it logs and returns -ENOENT (no node reference to release). Otherwise it reads opal-msg-async-num; if absent it logs, releases the node with of_node_put and returns -ENOENT. Else it stores the value in opal_max_async_tokens (a global that stays set even if a later step fails) and allocates opal_async_tokens with kcalloc; on failure it releases the node and returns -ENOMEM. Then it calls opal_message_notifier_register(OPAL_MSG_ASYNC_COMP, &opal_async_comp_nb); on a nonzero error it logs, kfree()s opal_async_tokens (the pointer is not reset to NULL), releases the node and returns that error. On success it calls sema_init(&opal_async_sem, opal_max_async_tokens), releases the node and returns 0.
note: Contract removed. Old prose said the node reference is released in every failure case; wrong for node-not-found (opal-async.c:252-257 goes to out, skipping of_node_put, node is NULL). Reviewer 15 only about contract. Slice cut head; real function at 246-290.

name: opal_sys_param_init
prose: Init function (void return) that creates sysfs files under opal_kobj for the OPAL system parameters described in /ibm,opal/sysparams. It returns early with no effect if opal_kobj is NULL (logs a warning) or if the /ibm,opal/sysparams node is absent. If the node is not compatible with ibm,opal-sysparams it logs and drops the node reference. It creates the 'sysparams' kobject (sysparam_kobj), allocates a MAX_PARAM_DATA_LEN zeroed buffer param_data_buf, counts the param-name strings and allocates id, size, perm and attr arrays of that count, then reads the param-id, param-len and param-perm properties. Each failure in this sequence logs an error and unwinds through the goto labels, freeing exactly the allocations made so far, calling kobject_put(sysparam_kobj) once it exists, and of_node_put(sysparam). The loop skips any parameter whose size exceeds MAX_PARAM_DATA_LEN or whose name cannot be read, sets the mode from the low two bits of perm (0444, 0200 or 0644; left unset for other values), and calls sysfs_create_file; if that fails it logs and unwinds through out_free_attr, freeing attr, perm, size, id, param_data_buf, putting the kobject (which removes files already created) and dropping the node reference. On success it frees perm, size, id, drops the node reference, and keeps attr, param_data_buf and sysparam_kobj allocated. The function never reports an error to its caller.
note: Slice (262-294) is the tail of opal_sys_param_init (opal-sysparam.c:143-~295); the listed name unnamed_init_function does not exist, so fixed under the real name per HAND_METHOD rule 6. Old prose (each goto frees exactly the resources acquired so far) is true.

name: set_subcores_per_core
prose: Changes the split-core mode to new_mode. If kvm_hv_mode_active() is true it logs an error and returns -EBUSY before doing anything else. Otherwise it does BUG_ON(new_mode < 1 || new_mode > 4 || new_mode == 3), so a value other than 1, 2 or 4 crashes the kernel (this check comes after the KVM check). It then sets state->step = SYNC_STEP_INITIAL and state->master = 0 in the per-CPU split_state of every present CPU, takes cpus_read_lock, sets master = 1 for the current CPU, issues mb(), calls stop_machine_cpuslocked(cpu_update_split_mode, &new_mode, cpu_online_mask) (its return value is ignored), releases cpus_read_lock, and returns 0. The globals that record the new mode are updated by the cpu_update_split_mode callback, which this entry did not read. There is no lock around the function; the comment states it is only called at boot or from a sysfs write.
note: Contract removed (global state, BUG_ON). No substantive reviewer disagreement (only mechanical); code checked at subcore.c:338-374. Slice cut head.

name: pseries_calculate_stolen_time
prose: Returns the stolen time (timebase ticks) accumulated up to stop_tb. It returns 0 if the firmware lacks FW_FEATURE_SPLPAR, and returns 0 if get_paca()->dtl_ridx equals be64_to_cpu(get_lppaca()->dtl_idx). Otherwise it returns scan_dispatch_log(stop_tb). That helper (which the comment says must be called with interrupts disabled) itself returns 0 without changing anything if local_paca->dtl_curr is NULL or if the read index already equals the VPA dtl_idx; in the other case it sums enqueue_to_dispatch_time plus ready_to_enqueue_time over the entries whose timebase is not after stop_tb (skipping ahead if the buffer overflowed), calls dtl_consumer for each entry under CONFIG_DTL when set, and then stores the new dtl_ridx and dtl_curr in the paca. No lock is taken.
note: Reviewer 15 (scan_dispatch_log returns early without advancing when dtl_curr is NULL) RIGHT: dtl.c:384-388. Reviewer 2 (caller must disable interrupts) consistent with the comment at dtl.c:372; stated as helper requirement. Contract was empty. Slice cut head; real function at 433-442 with helper at 374-415.

name: dlpar_memory_add_by_ic
prose: Hot-adds lmbs_to_add LMBs starting at DRC index drc_index. It logs the request, returns -EINVAL if lmbs_to_add is 0, calls get_lmb_range and returns -EINVAL if it fails, and returns -EINVAL if any LMB in the range has DRCONF_MEM_RESERVED set (logging that LMB). It then walks the range: LMBs already DRCONF_MEM_ASSIGNED are skipped; for each other LMB it calls dlpar_acquire_drc and breaks on error, then dlpar_add_lmb and, on error, calls dlpar_release_drc and breaks, otherwise marks the LMB reserved with drmem_mark_lmb_reserved. If a step failed it logs, walks the range again and, for each reserved LMB, calls dlpar_remove_lmb (logging if that fails, releasing the DRC with dlpar_release_drc if it succeeds) and removes the reservation, and the result is -EINVAL. If all steps succeeded it logs each reserved LMB as hot-added and clears its reservation, and the result is 0. It returns that result (0 or -EINVAL); no lock is taken in this function.
note: Contract removed (touches global LMB state). Reviewers (formal contract weaker than prose) concern old contract only; prose rechecked against code at hotplug-memory.c:736-807. Slice cut head.

name: enable_ddw
prose: Tries to set up a 64-bit DMA window for dev and returns a bool. Early part: it checks whether an ibm,pmemory node exists, takes dma_win_init_mutex, and jumps to out_unlock if find_existing_ddw finds an existing window for pdn (setting dev->dev.archdata.dma_offset and direct_mapping from it) or if pdn is on failed_ddw_pdn_list. Failures to read ibm,ddw-applicable, query_ddw, limited_dma_window, an in-use default table, a missing default window property, a failed ddw_read_ext reset check, a zero page_shift, create_ddw, or an unavailable window go to out_failed; the default window may be removed first (default_win_removed) when no windows are available. It computes the window length and sets dynamic_mapping/direct_mapping, creates the window with create_ddw, creates the property with ddw_property_create (failure: out_remove_win), adds it with of_add_property (failure: out_free_prop) and allocates a dma_win entry (failure: out_del_prop). For direct mapping it maps system RAM into the window (failure cleans the window and goes to out_del_list); if the default window was removed it drops tables[0] and clears the device table base. For dynamic mapping it allocates and initialises a new iommu table stored in tables[default_win_removed ? 0 : 1] and set as the device table base (allocation failure goes to out_del_list). It then, if the default window was removed, copies ibm,dma-window to ibm,dma-window-saved when that does not exist and removes ibm,dma-window, adds the new entry to dma_win_list under dma_win_list_lock, sets dma_offset to the window address and goes to out_unlock. The error labels undo the steps completed so far; out_failed also calls reset_dma_window when the default window was removed or limited addressing was enabled, and records pdn in failed_ddw_pdn_list when allocation of the record succeeds. out_unlock releases the mutex, may set dev->dev.bus_dma_limit if pmem is present with direct mapping and len != MAX_PHYSMEM_BITS, logs, and returns direct_mapping. direct_mapping is assigned before create_ddw, so the function can return true after a later failure (for example create_ddw or of_add_property failing) as well as on success; it returns false when it never reached that assignment or chose a dynamic-only window.
note: Reviewer 15 (returns direct_mapping so can return true after create_ddw/of_add_property failure) RIGHT: iommu.c:1565-1569 set direct_mapping before create_ddw at 1578 and out_unlock returns it at 1784. Old prose claimed false on any failure; fixed. Slice cut head; real function at 1447-1784.

name: spapr_tce_create_table
prose: Creates (or restores) the TCE window number num for a VFIO group and returns a long status. Before locking it returns -EINVAL if window_size is not a power of two or levels > 1. It then takes dma_win_init_mutex, finds the parent node (failure: -ENODEV via out_failed, which tries to record pdn in failed_ddw_pdn_list), returns -ENODEV through out_unlock (without recording) if pdn is already on the failed list, and allocates tbl with iommu_pseries_alloc_table (failure: -ENODEV via out_unlock). For num == 0, if the request is not for the default window and a DDW already exists it returns -EPERM; if it is a default-window request and ibm,dma-window is missing it also returns -EPERM when a DDW exists, otherwise restores the default window (restore_default_dma_window), builds tbl from the restored property, stores it in tables[0], unlocks and returns 0 through exit without creating a DDW. Otherwise it reads ibm,ddw-applicable (failure: that error through out_failed), calls query_ddw (failure: out_failed), returns -EINVAL through out_unlock if the largest available block is too small for the window, calls create_ddw (failure: -ENODEV via out_failed), creates and adds the window property and a dma_win entry, initialises tbl for the new window, stores it in tables[num], sets the device table base and dma_offset, adds the entry to dma_win_list, unlocks and goes to exit. Error paths remove the property or window created so far; the mutex is released in all paths that took it, and tbl is not freed on error paths in this function. On success (exit) it allocates the userspace view with pseries_tce_iommu_userspace_view_alloc, sets tbl->it_allocated_size, sets *ptbl = iommu_tce_table_get(tbl) (a reference for the caller) and returns 0.
note: Reviewer 1 (failure paths do not add to failed list / roll back) PARTLY RIGHT: out_failed records pdn but the -EPERM, -EINVAL (block too small) and tbl-alloc failure paths go to out_unlock directly. Reviewer 2 (default-window success returns 0 without DDW) right, stated. Reviewer 3 (early -EINVAL before mutex_lock) RIGHT: iommu.c:2081-2082 precedes 2086. Slice cut head; real function at 2059-2259.
